sentences.text:
Pawan vs State Of U.P. And Another on 10 February, 2025
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2025:Ahc:18857
Court No. - 74
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 2327 of 2025
Applicant :- Pawan

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Girijesh Kumar Gupta,Shiv Shankar Pd Gupta
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Vikas Budhwar,J.
1.

Heard Sri Girijesh Kumar Gupta, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Kuldeep Singh Chauhan, learned AGA for the State/opposite party no.1.
2.

Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that though a first information report stood lodged against the applicant being Criminal Case No. 489 of 2000 purported to be under Section under Sections 420, 467, 468. 471, IPC against the applicant his father and others however the entire allegations relates to a property dispute whereby suit was also instituted by first informant faction and proceedings under Section 145 of the Cr.P.C. was initiated by the father of the applicants since deceased.

He further submits that the charge sheet stood submitted on 14.2.2001 and cognizance order was issued on 18.5.2001 but the applicant is not stationed in Hapur pursuant whereto he has no information and he is 61 years of age.
He further submits that whatever allegations if would be (though doubtful) upon the father of the applicant since deceased but the applicant cannot be said to be have committed any offence.

He next submits that in a mechanical manner cognizance order has been issued and in furtherance thereof proceedings under Section 82 and 83 of the Cr.P.C. have also been initiated Pawan vs State Of U.P. And Another on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77254764/
1 3.

entities.text: Pawan vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned AGA on the other hand submits that the explanation set-forth in the application for non-presence emanating to non-bailable warrant and proceedings under Sections 82 and 83 of the Cr.P.C. are thoroughly improbable and unbelievable for the simple reason that the applicant stood marked as an accused in the FIR.

He further submits that whatever arguments the applicant seeks to raise the same can only be contested either in a trial or he should prefer an appropriate application before the Court below either for recalling and also for bail.
4. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

5. Considering the submissions of the parties and the arguments so sought to be advanced the Court is of the opinion that cognizance order is dated 18.5.2021 proceedings for non bailable warrant coupled with Sections 82 and 83 of the Cr.P.C. have already been initiated way back and the applicant has approached in the year 2025.
Further these are the differences which the applicant seeks to raise.

It is for the applicant to approach the court below by filing an appropriate application as permissible and advisable under law with the Court belief that the same shall be decided with most expedition strictly in accordance with law.
6. With the present observation, the present application under section 482 Cr.P.C. stands consigned to record.
